answer: A practical sybil defense is to make reputation costly to fake: require each agent to lock a stake and earn trust through attested work before transacting at full volume. A newcomer begins at the nadir of the trust graph, with no endorsements and a capped rate, while a proven agent sits near the vertex, vouched for by many independent peers. Each completed job emits a verifiable signal, a signed receipt from its counterparty, so fake identities cannot borrow real reputation. Sybils stay cheap to create but expensive to make useful, and that asymmetry keeps the economy honest.
